inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (6,946M). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the ~$10B 2026 buyback is the cash mechanism that funds that and more, and Q3 buybacks are left out of both the share count and the cash (value-neutral at a price near IV).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow add-back from Metrics.csv StockBasedComp ($536M). AT&T does not tag withholding tax on net-share settlement separately in XBRL, so no equity-award-tax uplift; SBC is 0.4% of revenue, so the omission is worth well under $0.10/share.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~8.5% (US 10y ~4.25% + beta ~0.8 x 5.0% ERP + small leverage premium); after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (FY2025 interest incurred $7.0B on ~$135B book debt = 5.2% pre-tax, 22% tax). Market-value weights ~52% equity ($169B) / 48% debt+NCI ($157B pro forma) give ~6.3%; rounded UP to 7.0% because the debt stack reprices upward as ~$9B/yr matures and the EchoStar deal lifts leverage to ~3x. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the driver paths and weights, not a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost sits inside EBITDA and OCF, so leases are in the flows; operating lease liabilities ($22.5B FY2025) are therefore NOT in net debt. Finance leases ($1.4B) are inside book debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated, so the $15,990M noncontrolling interest (Jun-2026 balance sheet; mostly Telco LLC preferred interests carrying ~$1.4B/yr of distributions) is deducted at book in the equity bridge. Charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), 10-year horizon. AT&T is a pure-play US connectivity operating company after the 2022 WarnerMedia spin and DIRECTV exit - not a bank, REIT or holdco - so the routing table sends it to owner-FCF; no prior DCF and no memory entry exist, so this is a fresh build. Mid-cycle normalisation: the explicit years carry the guided $23-24B capital investment (capex + vendor-financing payments, ~18% of revenue, above the 16.6% cash-capex line in the CSV because AT&T's FCF definition also deducts vendor-financing payments) through the fiber build to 60M passings by 2030, then fade network capex to ~15%. SPECTRUM: spectrum purchases sit outside capex but are a recurring owner cost (AWS-3 2015, C-band 2021, 3.45GHz 2022, EchoStar $23B 2026 = ~$6B/yr average over a decade); the EchoStar payment (closed 2026-07-28) is deducted in the bridge and a normalised spectrum charge of 1.0-1.5pp of revenue (base), 0.5-1.0pp (bull), 2.0-2.5pp (bear) is folded into capex_pct_path from 2029 (upper C-band auction). DEBT: Metrics.csv TotalDebt (143,954 at Q2-26) double-counts the current portion - XBRL LongTermDebt (134,718 at FY2025) already includes debt maturing within one year and ties to face 144,311 less 9,193 unamortised discount; total debt used = 143,954 - 9,323 = 134,631. CASH TAX: FY2025 cash tax $1.35B and H1-26 $91M reflect OBBBA 100% bonus depreciation on a capex-heavy base; ramped 3% -> 22% (21% federal + net state) by FY2033. Year-1 build gives ~$22B unlevered owner FCF; less ~$7.5B after-tax-ish interest that is ~$15-16B levered vs the $18B+ guide - the ~$2B gap is device-receivable/working-capital timing that is not projected as recurring (conservative). Buybacks: active repurchaser ($4.5B FY2025, $4.7B H1-26, ~$10B 2026 target) so the flat count is genuinely funded.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (low-single-digit service revenue growth through 2028; H1-26 revenue +2.6% YoY), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every 5-year CAGR is divestiture-distorted: FY2020-21 include WarnerMedia (spun April 2022) and DIRECTV, so revenue (-2.6%), equity (-6.7%) and owner FCF (-7.6%) describe a different company. EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY2020 and FY2022 GAAP losses from impairments). The 3-year equity CAGR (5.9%) is inflated by FY2025 gains on the DIRECTV and tower sales. Guidance-based 2.5% is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - SBC; interest income not deducted (net debt). FY2022 OCF/FCF is missing from the CSV, so the 3-year FCF CAGR is null; FY2023 owner FCF $19,982M -> FY2025 $18,906M is -2.7%/yr, the result of capex stepping up for fiber, not of SBC (SBC flat at ~$0.5B).

base.capex_note: Capital investment incl. vendor financing; 2026 = $23.2B (guide $23-24B). Network capex fades to ~15% after the 2030 fiber target; +1.0pp spectrum from FY2029 rising to +1.5pp terminal.
base.ebitda_note: FY2026 adj. EBITDA +3.5% (guide 3-4%), FY2027 +4.5%, FY2028 ~+5% (guide 5%+) as copper retires; plateau 38.5%, between Verizon (~36%) and T-Mobile (~38-39%).

bull.capex_note: Fiber build finishes on budget with JV partners funding part of it; network capex ~14.5% plus 1.0pp spectrum.

bear.capex_note: Competitive pressure keeps network capex ~15.5% and spectrum costs ~2.0-2.5pp (expensive upper C-band, satellite/FWA forcing more capacity spend).

scenario_narratives.base: Management's multi-year framework roughly delivered: low-single-digit service revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA +3.5% in 2026 accelerating to ~5% by 2028 as legacy copper is decommissioned and fiber penetration scales toward 60M passings, then a plateau at a 38.5% margin. Capital investment stays at ~$23-24B through the build, then network capex fades while a recurring spectrum charge (~1.5% of revenue) replaces the EchoStar-type lumps. Cash taxes rise from the OBBBA-depressed ~3% to a normal 22%. Wireless share holds near the improved Q2-26 run-rate (432K postpaid phone adds, 0.86% churn) without T-Mobile or Verizon starting a price war.
scenario_narratives.bull: Convergence proves a structural margin lever: 42-45% bundle attach compounds as fiber reaches 60M+ passings, churn stays sub-0.9%, EchoStar spectrum lets AT&T take share at lower incremental capex, and the Business Wireline copper drag disappears faster than guided once California-style carrier-of-last-resort obligations fall away. Revenue grows ~3.5% mid-decade, EBITDA margin reaches 40%, network capex settles near 14.5% with JV partners (Gigapower, Forged Fiber 37) carrying part of the build, and spectrum needs stay modest.
scenario_narratives.bear: Wireless reverts to a promotional share fight (T-Mobile momentum, Verizon-Frontier convergence, Boost riding AT&T's own network as a hybrid MNO), legacy Business Wireline goes EBITDA-negative after 2027 as management itself warned and copper retirement is slowed by state carrier-of-last-resort disputes, and Starlink direct-to-cell plus fixed wireless erode rural fiber returns. Revenue grows ~1%, margin stalls near 36%, and capex never comes down because spectrum (an expensive upper C-band auction) and capacity spend replace fiber spend. Leverage near 3x keeps the refinancing bill high but solvency is not in question.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from 15%): ~3x leverage after EchoStar, a three-way wireless market where AT&T has historically lagged, and management's own warning that legacy wireline turns EBITDA-negative after 2027. Base 55%: guidance has been met or beaten for several years and the business is low-cyclicality subscription revenue. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs share gains, margin expansion AND a capex fade to happen together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on an unlevered basis at a 7% USD WACC, with every cost an owner actually bears charged once: SBC in the flows, vendor-financing payments inside capital investment, a normalised spectrum charge for the purchases AT&T's own FCF definition leaves out, the EchoStar cash in the bridge, preferred-like NCI and postemployment obligations deducted at book. The ~$18B 'FCF' headline is levered and excludes spectrum; it is not the owner's cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is capped at 12-15x terminal FCF; at a 7% WACC Gordon would be ~20x, so the cap is doing real work and the value is sensitive to it.
Spectrum normalisation (1-2.5pp of revenue) is judgment; each 1pp of revenue is ~$1.3B/yr, roughly $2.5-3/share.
Equity is ~half of EV; each 1% change in EV moves equity value ~2%.
Cash-tax ramp: if 100% bonus depreciation persists and capex stays above D&A, the 22% terminal cash rate is conservative.
Debt figure: Metrics.csv TotalDebt double-counts the current portion; this build uses XBRL book debt (~$134.6B) - using the CSV figure would understate value by ~$1.35/share.
